one_liner: Compact, portable embeddable ES5.1 JavaScript interpreter in C; about 1.6x MuJS on Linux/macOS, about half QuickJS's speed.
what_it_does: Duktape is a JavaScript engine you embed in a C or C++ program by adding three files from the release tarball (duktape.c, duktape.h, duk_config.h) and calling a Lua-like value-stack C API (duk_create_heap, duk_peval_string, duk_push_*/duk_get_*). It implements ECMAScript 5.1 with selected ES2015+ features (TypedArray, Node.js Buffer, Proxy subset), a built-in debugger protocol, bytecode dump/load, coroutines and an optional CommonJS module loader. Its API is its own, so it is not a drop-in for MuJS or QuickJS.
how_it_is_fast: It is footprint-first rather than speed-first: a register-based bytecode interpreter (doc/execution.rst) with no JIT, reference counting plus mark-and-sweep for tight memory, and configure.py options that trade size for speed. The relevant speed option is DUK_USE_FASTINT (48-bit integer fast path, off by default, on in the benchmarked Linux/macOS build), which explains most of its lead over MuJS on the integer-heavy Crypto test (1022 vs 241 on ubuntu); the guide also recommends PGO (about 20% for GCC -O2).
when_to_use: Embedding a scripting layer in a C/C++ application or firmware where binary size and portability matter more than speed: the stripped duk command-line binary is 370.4K on ubuntu, versus 2.2M for QuickJS, and Duktape has the best Score/MB of every engine in the ubuntu table (1885).
Targets that only have a C89 compiler (plus snprintf/vsnprintf), exotic CPUs or 32-bit pointers, where its packed 8-byte value representation (DUK_USE_PACKED_TVAL) keeps memory use low.
When you need ES5.1 compliance plus a remote debugger protocol and bytecode caching, and you control the scripts that run.
As a faster alternative to MuJS for numeric or object-heavy scripts on Linux or macOS (Crypto, Splay, NavierStokes rows), provided you build with fastint.
when_not_to_use: Throughput-sensitive scripting: QuickJS scores about 2.2x higher on ubuntu (1522 vs 682), 2.0x on macOS arm64 (1672 vs 842) and 3.0x on windows (1105 vs 371), and quickjs-ng is also ahead; Duktape has no JIT.
Modern JavaScript: the README promises ES5.1 with only partial ES2015/ES2016 support, so ES2017+ features such as async/await need transpiling first.

Regex-heavy workloads: Duktape's RegExp row is its weakest and MuJS beats it on all three platforms (ubuntu 184 vs 251, macOS 224 vs 282, windows 104 vs 192); open issue #334 notes slow case-insensitive Unicode regexps.
Random access into long non-ASCII strings: character-offset lookups scan the UTF-8/WTF-8 bytes behind a small string cache (open issue #335 proposes an index).
Running untrusted bytecode, or depending on the 3.x master branch for production: master is undergoing incompatible changes and the 2.x line (v2-maintenance) has had no commit since 2022-07-24.

integration.form: source-drop (amalgamated duktape.c + duktape.h + duk_config.h from the release tarball); custom configurations are generated with tools/configure.py
integration.dependencies: none at run time beyond libc and libm (the Date built-in may need a platform provider); configure.py needs Python with PyYAML
integration.min_toolchain: C89 compiler with snprintf()/vsnprintf() (guide, Portability); also compiles as C++; the repo Makefile builds with -std=c99
integration.platforms: any platform with such a compiler: Linux, macOS (including arm64 in CI), Windows (MinGW and MSVC), embedded and 32-bit targets; LoongArch support added on master in 2024
integration.thread_safety: One native thread at a time per Duktape heap (application must lock, or use duk_suspend/duk_resume to hand over); separate heaps are fully isolated and can run concurrently.

gotchas: Benchmark harness: the ahaoboy CI installs Duktape from ahaoboy/duktape-build's only release (v0.1.0, built 2025-06-19 from master, which had no commits between 2024-01-29 and 2026-09-04), so the binary is unchanged between daily runs; its ubuntu score still moved from 489 (10/5/2026 snapshot) to 682 (10/11/2026), about 39%, and QuickJS moved from 1217 to 1522 in the same window, so single runs on shared GitHub runners carry noise larger than the 1.09x windows margin over MuJS.

The three platforms run different Duktape builds: ubuntu and macOS use master (2.99.99) built with util/makeduk_base.yaml (DUK_USE_FASTINT on, plus interrupt counter, debugger support and self tests), while windows uses release 2.7.0 built with Makefile.cmdline and the default config, where DUK_USE_FASTINT defaults to false; that is why windows Crypto is 309 against 1022 on ubuntu and why the windows lead over MuJS nearly disappears.

Score is the geometric mean of the eight per-test scores (recomputed: 681.5 and 435.4 from the ubuntu rows), not a sum. Leaving out Crypto and NavierStokes, Duktape over MuJS drops to about 1.29x on ubuntu and 1.27x on macOS, and MuJS leads about 1.13x on windows (derived from page data).

Duktape does not validate loaded bytecode; its guide warns that crafted bytecode can lead to exploitable memory-unsafe behavior. A WebSearch snippet of NVD's CVE-2026-12216 (count_instr in the bytecode loader, up to 2.99.99) says Debian lists 2.7.0-2 as unfixed. Master also carried a heap-buffer-overflow in the backwards WTF-8 string-cache scanner until PR #2587 (merged 2026-09-04), so the benchmarked master build predates that fix.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Duktape over QuickJS when binary size and C89-level portability matter more than about 2x throughput and ES2020+ features, and over MuJS when your scripts are numeric or object-heavy rather than regex-heavy; for microcontroller-class memory budgets also compare JerryScript (lower peak memory in its issue #4386 table) and XS (Moddable).
verified_claims_summary: In ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark (V8 v7 suite from arewefastyet, one run per engine on GitHub-hosted runners with unstated CPUs, README snapshot 10/11/2026), the Duktape command-line binary scores 682 vs MuJS 435 on ubuntu, 842 vs 522 on macOS arm64 (both Duktape master built with gcc/clang -Os and fastint) and 371 vs 339 on windows (release 2.7.0, MinGW gcc -Os, no fastint), while QuickJS scores 1522/1672/1105; the binaries are stripped by the harness and compiler versions are not stated.
status_note: MIT-licensed and easy to vendor, but maintenance is thin: the last release is 2.7.0 (February 2022), v2-maintenance has been idle since 2022-07-24, and master (unreleased 3.x, incompatible changes in progress) received only one merged fix between January 2024 and September 2026, so the record's 'active' status overstates it; vendor 2.7.0 and apply security fixes yourself.
